title: SEC Company Directory
description: Optional credential: SEC_EDGAR_CONTACT overrides the default SEC fair-access User-Agent. SEC EDGAR doesn't issue API keys - it just wants a reachable email in the User-Agent string. Leave it unset and the script uses the SpeakesQuery default; set it (e.g. "your.name@example.com") to supply your own contact. Fetches the complete SEC EDGAR company tickers directory - every publicly traded company with their CIK number, ticker symbol, and exchange. This is the foundational reference dataset for all SEC analysis. Useful as a lookup table for cross-referencing company data across other scripts. Over 10,000 companies indexed.
code:
import pandas as pd
import requests
from datetime import datetime, timezone

contact = (CREDENTIALS.get('SEC_EDGAR_CONTACT') or '').strip()
if not contact or '@' not in contact:
    # SEC EDGAR's fair-access policy accepts any User-Agent that contains
    # a reachable email - it is NOT an API key / authentication token. Fall
    # back to the project default so scheduled SEC jobs run out of the box;
    # users can override by setting SEC_EDGAR_CONTACT in Settings → Credentials.
    contact = 'SpeakesQuery EDGAR (noreply@speakesquery.local)'
HEADERS = {'User-Agent': contact}
now_epoch = int(datetime.now(timezone.utc).timestamp())

resp = requests.get(
    'https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json',
    headers=HEADERS,
    timeout=30,
)
resp.raise_for_status()
data = resp.json()

rows = []
keys = list(data.keys())
for k in keys:
    entry = data[k]
    cik = int(entry.get('cik_str', 0))
    rows.append({
        'cik': cik,
        'cik_padded': str(cik).zfill(10),
        'ticker': str(entry.get('ticker', '')).upper(),
        'company_name': entry.get('title', ''),
        '_epoch': now_epoch,
    })

df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
if not df.empty:
    df = df.sort_values('cik').reset_index(drop=True)
GENERATE_RESULTS(df)
